Complete thermal processes developed over six decades and proven in production fabs worldwide.

Diffusion processes modify the electrical properties of wafer material by introducing dopant atoms from a chemical vapor source or by annealing crystal defects. Tempress offers high-temperature annealing up to 1365°C, wet and dry oxidation, phosphorus and boron doping with POCl3 and BBr3, plus lower-temperature sintering, alloying and annealing with up to 100% H2.

Deposition processes produce thin films of high-quality solid materials on a wafer. Tempress offers Low Pressure CVD (LPCVD) for improved uniformity, Plasma Enhanced CVD (PECVD) for lower-temperature processing with higher deposition rates, and Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) for ultra-thin, conformal films with atomic-level thickness control.

The AVP Ace is an advanced vertical batch furnace for 150 mm and 200 mm wafers. It delivers excellent process performance, optimized cost of ownership, and outstanding flexibility for diffusion, oxidation, and LPCVD applications. Building on proven process modules and an updated control architecture, the AVP Ace can be configured to meet specific production and engineering requirements.

The RVP Ace is a high-productivity vertical batch furnace for 200 mm and 300 mm wafers. It provides a flexible platform for diffusion, oxidation, and LPCVD processes, combining strong process performance with optimized cost of ownership. Proven process modules, updated controls, and flexible wafer-handling options enable the system to meet a wide range of production and engineering requirements.

An atmospheric diffusion process is a heat treatment in a mostly inert environment which distributes dopants in a silicon, GaAs, InP or other semiconductor wafer to a desired depth, changing the electrical properties of the semiconductor. Sometimes a reactive element such as oxygen is added, consuming silicon and converting it into silicon dioxide (SiO2) for use in many applications.

Low Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition uses a chemical reaction to convert gas phase precursors into useful films. The products of that reaction are deposited on top of the wafer and therefore do not consume atoms from the base material.

Tempress offers furnace solutions for various other processes such as wafer splitting (SOI/POI) and polyimide curing, and is open to customise and co-develop specific thermal processes to fit your needs.

Tempress supports specialty device manufacturers with configurable diffusion, oxidation, annealing and low-pressure deposition solutions. Horizontal and vertical batch platforms can be adapted to process requirements, wafer formats and production volumes, from process development and pilot lines through established manufacturing.

Power semiconductor devices handle high electrical currents or voltages with high efficiency. Diodes, thyristors, MOSFETs and IGBTs are essential to power transmission, renewable energy systems, industrial equipment and the electrification of transport.

Microelectromechanical systems typically contain structures between 1 and 100 micrometers and are widely used in accelerometers, gyroscopes, pressure sensors and other precision devices. Related manufacturing methods also create extremely small mechanical parts for applications such as high-end watchmaking.

For MEMS manufacturing, Tempress offers LPCVD silicon nitride, low-stress nitride, polysilicon and TEOS processes, together with surface treatment, PECVD, oxidation and annealing solutions. These process capabilities are used by established manufacturers and leading research institutes.

Tempress furnace systems are used by internationally recognized institutes and manufacturers to develop and produce photonic devices. Available process solutions include low-loss silicon nitride, polysilicon, thick thermal oxide and carefully controlled annealing for optical layers and device structures.

Wafer manufacturers use thermal processing to improve substrate quality, create engineered layers and add value before device fabrication. Annealing, wet and dry oxidation and LPCVD polysilicon are important steps in the production of advanced silicon and compound-material wafers.

Tempress supports packaging flows with lower-temperature deposition, annealing and polyimide curing processes. Flexible batch platforms help manufacturers establish repeatable film properties and thermal budgets for passivation, dielectric, bonding and through-silicon-via related applications.

The Internet of Things connects physical objects and devices so that their condition, location and use can be measured and acted upon. Applications range from ultra-low-cost identification and supply-chain tracking to sensors and connectivity chips used in phones, vehicles and industrial systems.

Light-emitting diodes and related optoelectronic devices are built on compound-semiconductor and engineered substrates that demand stable, repeatable thermal processing. Applications span general lighting, displays, automotive systems, sensing, ultraviolet sources and optical communication.

Tempress furnace platforms support annealing, oxidation and deposition steps for LED process development and manufacturing. Flexible temperature control, atmosphere management and batch configurations help address sapphire, silicon and compound-semiconductor substrate requirements.

Tempress works with industrial and research partners to adapt diffusion, deposition and controlled-atmosphere heat treatment to new substrates and materials. This collaborative approach helps move emerging processes from laboratory development toward stable, scalable production.
